column5: Imagine a long beach on a summer afternoon.
The sand is almost too hot to walk on.
Right now, every square meter of this beach receives about a thousand watts of sunlight.
All of it comes from one star, a hundred and fifty million kilometers away.
Now imagine that, without any warning, the Sun goes out.
Light needs eight minutes and twenty seconds to cross that distance.
So the sunshine on this beach is already on its way.
For eight minutes, the sea would keep sparkling, and nobody would know.
Then the last light would land.
In a few seconds, the afternoon would turn into night.
Stars would appear over the sea, in the middle of the day.
And the sand would slowly begin to give up its heat.
